test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 26 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following solutions will turn pH paper blue?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Sodium hydroxide__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A base is sodium hydroxide**.
 
• **Red litmus is changed to blue by the base.** Sodium hydroxide converts red litmus into blue in this way.
 
• Blue paper won't alter when exposed to a sodium hydroxide solution that is dilute.
 
• **Since sodium hydroxide (pH-12) is an alkali, it will cause the pH paper to turn blue.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Acid and Base**

 
 

 **Acid** 
 **Base**
 
 

 
 
 
• Acids have a **sour flavour**.
 
 
 
 
 
• Bases feel **soapy and have a bitter flavour.**
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
• Sour fruits, vinegar, toilet cleanser, sodium hydroxide, and other substances all include acids.
 
 
 
 
 
• Bases are found in things like neem, clove, and soaps.
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
• Acids cause the blue **litmus paper to turn red.**
 
 
 
 
 
• When bases are present, the **litmus paper becomes blue.**
